hypothesis: Late delivery is a major driver of negative reviews.
data_test: Mann-Whitney U + chi-square + odds ratio + bootstrap CI; logistic regression with controls
statistical_evidence: Mean score 2.27 (late) vs 4.29 (on time); dissatisfied 62.4% vs 9.3%; Cliff's delta -0.64 (large); OR 16.26; p<1e-300
note: Association only. Effect is much smaller when restricted to reviews written after delivery (see H1_sensitivity): many late-order reviews were created before the recorded delivery date.

hypothesis: Certain sellers have systematically poor customer experience.
data_test: Chi-square homogeneity across sellers (>=50 orders); Wilson CI vs overall rate
statistical_evidence: chi2=2167.0, dof=412, p=1.8e-235, Cramer's V=0.174; 52 of 413 sellers have CI lower bound above overall rate

hypothesis: Some product categories have unusually high complaint rates.
data_test: Chi-square homogeneity across categories (>=100 orders); Wilson CI
statistical_evidence: chi2=464.0, dof=51, p=5.7e-68, V=0.070; 9 of 52 categories significantly worse

hypothesis: High freight costs are associated with poor customer satisfaction.
data_test: Spearman correlation + top vs bottom quartile Mann-Whitney
statistical_evidence: Spearman rho=-0.031 (p=7.8e-22); top-vs-bottom quartile Cliff's delta -0.043 (negligible)
verdict: Statistically significant but negligible practical effect
note: Statistical significance is not the same as practical importance; check effect size.
